primary_source.title: GAUSS: A Workload-Aware Analytical and Monte-Carlo Simulator for LLM Inference Serving

verified_claims_and_metrics.document_type: 10-page analytical methodology and tutorial technical report

symbolic_formulation.workload_buckets: bucket j = (s_j input tokens, c_j cached prefix tokens, o_j output tokens) with probability weight w_j, sum_j w_j = 1
symbolic_formulation.arrival_process: Poisson process of mean rate lambda (inter-arrival A ~ Exp(lambda))
symbolic_formulation.chunked_prefill: n = ceil((s - c) / Delta); g_i = c + i*Delta; l_i = a + b*g_i; L_pre(s, c) = a*n + b*sigma where sigma = n*c + Delta*n*(n+1)/2 (quadratic in chunk count n)
symbolic_formulation.decode_batch_surface: d(B, C) = p + q*(C/B) + r*B (piecewise across batch-size regimes in practice)
symbolic_formulation.capacity_and_service_rate: E[S] = sum_j w_j * S(s_j, c_j); mu = 1 / E[S]; stability rho = lambda/mu < 1; sustainable ceiling lambda* = mu
symbolic_formulation.lindley_recurrence: W_{k+1} = max(0, W_k + S_k - A_k) across k = 1..M into delay sample pool Q
symbolic_formulation.ttft_and_tbt: TTFT_i = W + S(s, c); TBT_i = d(B, C)/eta inflated by interleaved prefill chunks averaged over generated tokens o; operating B solved from a closed-form quadratic
symbolic_formulation.hol_blocking_formula: E[W] = lambda * E[S^2] / (2*(1 - rho)) (Pollaczek-Khinchin M/G/1 mean wait motivating context-length segmentation)

section_4_use_cases: 4.1 Operating-point selection below the TTFT tail knee and headroom quantification against lambda* = mu
4.2 Context-length traffic segmentation optimizing candidate boundaries via analytical E[S] and E[S^2]
4.3 Closed-form remaining chunked-prefill work estimation for SRPT scheduling
4.4 Ensemble Monte-Carlo estimation vs. single-trace time averaging for fleet headroom routing and hardware/engine what-if analysis

explicit_limitations: arXiv:2610.37989v1 contains zero empirical calibration values for (a, b, p, q, r, eta, Delta), zero named GPU/accelerator experiments, and zero measured TTFT/TBT prediction error comparisons against real engines (e.g., vLLM, Sarathi-Serve) or discrete-event simulators (e.g., Vidur).

Section 1 and Section 2.3 motivate GAUSS with bursty arrivals (citing BurstGPT and Cox processes), whereas Section 3 restricts the baseline formulation to stationary Poisson arrivals (A ~ Exp(lambda)) and static bucket weights w_j, which can underpredict queue tails under clustered bursts (CV^2 > 1).

Algorithm 1 models admission as a single-server FIFO M/G/1 queue without HBM KV-cache exhaustion/preemption checks, without a modified non-FIFO queueing recurrence for Section 4.3 SRPT scheduling, and without prefill-decode disaggregation, MoE routing, speculative decoding, or multi-node parallelism.

The v1 text omits closed-form algebraic expressions for the operating batch-size B quadratic (§3.8), load-coupled concurrent decode step d_bar, chunk-TBT inflation term (Algorithm 1 line 325), piecewise d(B, C) breakpoints (§3.3), and Lindley burn-in/autocorrelation controls near rho -> 1.
